clue.text: The end for Mrs T cuts her up well and good?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: final letter of Mrs

indicators.note: something that cuts into another thing lodges inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: her refers to Mrs T, Margaret Thatcher, so it stands for her first name
taken as written; it cuts into the name, after MARGAR

explanation.surface: A question about Margaret Thatcher's downfall: did those who cut her up do so for her own good?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits as 'Mrs' and 'T', not 'Mrs T': S, then MARGARET with T inside, all reversed gives TETRAGRAMS. Mrs T is Margaret Thatcher, the British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is a four-letter word, and 'well' and 'good' are examples, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Yen to follow opsimath's debut novel with a single

indicators.note: a thing set to follow others comes after them, so this piece is placed at the end
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of the word before it is taken

parts.note: first letter of opsimath
novel means new
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency; 'to follow' puts it last

explanation.surface: A late learner's first novel, with a longing to follow it up with a hit single record.
explanation.walkthrough: An opsimath is someone who learns late in life. 'Yen to follow' places Y after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a single is a ticket for travel in one direction only, a one-way ticket.

clue.text: Sadly little delight in "big" trip, so from time to time say so!

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of little are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
to delight in something is to like it

indicators.note: only now and then, so just every other letter of the words is taken

parts.note: the even letters of these words give ITIS

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about a disappointing holiday, ending with an exhortation to be candid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges LITTLE as TELLIT; 'from time to time' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of big trip so.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell it like it is means to speak bluntly and honestly, to say so plainly.

clue.text: Husband has gone to work to pen me another fancy song

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one group of letters goes inside the other
gone set to work is gone reworked, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: fancy as a verb-like modifier means elaborated or altered, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A husband has left for work, leaving his partner to compose another elaborate song.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams are at work: 'gone to work' is one, 'me another fancy' the other, and the second is penned inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Home on the Range is a classic American cowboy ballad, the state song of Kansas.

clue.text: Equatorial finale of Love's Labour's Lost?

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: final letter of Love's

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters before it wander out of order

parts.note: letters of Labour's rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about how Shakespeare's comedy Love's Labour's Lost ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's title splits into three jobs: one letter from Love's, Labour's as letters to rearrange, and Lost as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsolar means lying directly beneath the sun, which happens only in the tropical band around the equator.

clue.text: Called out where ship may secure small weight

indicators.note: called out means spoken aloud, so the clue gives words heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a ship ties up at a quay; low can mean small, as in a low number

explanation.surface: Shouting out where a boat might moor to a small anchor-weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram, often shortened, is the standard metric unit of mass.

clue.text: May record together?

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of the current month, and the puzzle appeared in May
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone called May might record an album with others.
explanation.walkthrough: Old business letters wrote 'the 3rd inst.' for the 3rd of this month; this puzzle ran on 3 May, so May was the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: People in step move in unison, keeping pace with one another, so are together.

clue.text: Village maypole central to such cultivated movement?

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a maypole stands on the village green, and dancers circle it, so it is the centre of a turning on the green
surface reading: a cultivated movement is an agricultural campaign, the farming change of the twentieth century

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer is a rotation on a village green, which a maypole sits at the centre of.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to the post-war spread of high-yield crops and modern farming in developing countries.

clue.text: In character of which bazoo's opening will stop silences

definitions.text: In character of which bazoo's opening will stop silences

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these pieces fill the middle of the following word

parts.note: gags silence people; they are split around the next pieces
as means in the character of, as in acting as a judge

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its start, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of bazoo, a slang word for the mouth

explanation.surface: Describes characters whose mouths, once opened, will put an end to any silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: talkers fill every silence once their mouths open. Bazoo is old American slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasbags are people who talk endlessly, so their talk breaks every pause in conversation.

clue.text: Writer shifts bed, fracturing wrist badly

indicators.note: fracturing means breaking open, so the rearranged letters are split apart to admit others
badly means in a damaged way, so the letters of wrist are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
shifts as a verb means changes, or alters
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone moves a bed and injures their wrist in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: WRIST jumbled ('badly') gives SIRWT, broken apart by ALTERS and COT to give SIR W-ALTERSCOT-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott was the Scottish novelist and poet who wrote Ivanhoe and Waverley.

clue.text: See 9
Temper fraying if this?

indicators.note: to temper something is to modify or mix it, so the letters of the next word are remixed

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
taken as written; with the answer it makes up the remixed letters, so it is taken away

explanation.surface: Asks whether your temper would be fraying if you were in this state.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged fraying equals 'if' plus 'this', the answer; take away 'if' and five letters remain. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone angry is losing patience, which is exactly what a fraying temper describes.

clue.text: I'm leaving a pointer from the Kennel Club for Spooner …

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.words: a pointer from the Kennel Club
parts.note: a poodle is a breed recognised by the Kennel Club, and a tip is a pointer or hint

explanation.surface: Someone takes their leave with a piece of advice from the dog-breeding body.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kennel Club is the UK body that registers dog breeds. Swapping the opening sounds of poodle tip gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye, what you say on leaving.

clue.text: See 4
Campaigners of course upstanding to welcome top constituent

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the outer letters hold the rest
in a down clue, standing up means the letters read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: yep is a casual yes, of course; turned up it reads PEY and opens around the rest
ace means top, excellent
a constituent is a part of something

explanation.surface: Campaigners naturally stand up to greet a leading voter in their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed casual yes, PEY, wraps the words for top and constituent.
explanation.definitionFit: A peace party is a group of people working or lobbying for peace, so a body of campaigners.

clue.text: … this dog represented in ideographs

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters of ideographs are rearranged to show the answer and the named word together

parts.note: the fodder: its letters are the answer plus D, O, G
these three letters, together with the answer, make up the fodder

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a dog breed is depicted in Chinese characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DOG out of the letters of IDEOGRAPHS and the remaining seven rearrange into the answer, a Chinese breed, fitting the ideographs of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar pei is a wrinkled Chinese breed of dog, apt for something written in Chinese characters.

clue.text: Something Porky Pig's originator curiously can't eat

indicators.note: an originator comes at the start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of Pig

indicators.note: arranged curiously means set out in an odd way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters of can't eat rearranged

explanation.surface: Porky Pig's creator oddly cannot eat a certain food, perhaps out of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Porky Pig is the Looney Tunes cartoon pig; here Porky is an adjective, made of pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is Italian cured pork belly, so it is a porky item of food.

clue.text: On cycle run, beginning a ferocious race?

indicators.note: letters on a cycle go round, so letters from the front move to the back

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a start is a beginning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cycle race starting off at fierce speed is a ferocious race.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces make RSTARTA; moving its first two letters to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tartars were the Central Asian peoples of the Mongol hordes, reputed fierce, and a tartar is a fearsome person.

clue.text: Frankfurter might get stuck into this bread, hot large slices!

definitions.text: Frankfurter might get stuck into this bread

indicators.note: something that slices a word cuts into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hot goods are stolen goods
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sausage might be pushed into a bread roll, with hot large slices on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frankfurter' looks like a sausage but means someone from Frankfurt, who might tuck into German bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit bread eaten at Christmas, just what a German from Frankfurt might enjoy.

clue.text: Double batting — following on

parts.note: the side batting in cricket is in
since means following, after
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a batter on a double score, or a team made to follow on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' looks like a score or a cricket term but means two-faced. In cricket, following on means batting again straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Double here is the old adjective for deceitful, as in double-dealing, so insincere fits.

clue.text: Quotients worked out by university on this?

definitions.text: Quotients worked out by university on this?

indicators.note: letters worked out are reworked, so the word before is shuffled into new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
U is the abbreviation for university; taken away from the rearranged letters
taken as written; also taken away

explanation.surface: Asks whether a university would work out intelligence quotients on this exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged quotients equal U plus ON plus 'this', the answer; take away U and ON to leave it. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An IQ test is the exam from which an intelligence quotient score is calculated.

clue.text: Sort these Etonians will protect

indicators.note: to protect something is to shelter it inside, so the letters are tucked within the words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Pupils of Eton College promise to protect a certain sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English private school. 'Sort' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in sort out.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to a problem is to deal with it, to sort it out.

clue.text: Remix is done like a shot in studio

indicators.note: a remix of a track reorders its parts, so the following letters are reordered

parts.note: letters of is done rearranged

explanation.surface: A recording studio's remix is finished, done in one take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remix' and 'studio' suggest music, but the shot is a photograph or camera angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-on camera shot is taken from the side, a profile view of the subject.

clue.text: It'll have landed with engineering trouble

indicators.note: with engineering means contriving or rearranging, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A spacecraft or aircraft will touch down despite technical difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with engineering' looks like a description of the landing, but it tells you to rearrange the fourteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil and all is an old idiom for a great deal of difficulty or bother.

clue.text: A boost for the compiler being presented with his award

indicators.note: a boost lifts something up, and in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who calls himself me
the compiler's own word for his is my

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter gets a lift from receiving his own award.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the compiler or setter often stands for ME; speaking as the setter, his becomes my.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is the American television industry's annual prize, a statuette award.

clue.text: See 3
See 21
A great deal or a bad egg?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: very much, a British informal intensifier, as in 'I miss her terribly'
second meaning, taken literally: an egg gone off is a thing that has decayed

explanation.walkthrough: The British colloquial phrase 'I love her something rotten' means very much. 'Bad egg' usually means a villain, but here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as an informal adverb for 'enormously' and literally as a description of a putrid item like a spoiled egg.
